name: Dorle Hager
forbes_bio: Dorle Hager is a major shareholder of Hager Group.
The company is a leading provider of solutions and services for electrical installations, covering business fields such as energy distribution, cable management, and building automation.
Hager SE generates consolidated group revenues exceeding $3.5 billion annually.
Originally founded as a GmbH, the company has a history spanning over three decades and transitioned into a Societas Europaea (SE) in May 2007.
The group operates internationally with a workforce exceeding 13,000 employees and manages well-known brands such as Hager, Berker, and E3/DC.

name: Liu Baolin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2011-2023); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2008-2026)
forbes_bio: Liu Baolin chairs Jointown Pharmaceutical Group, an operator of pharmacies and wholesaler of pharmaceuticals and medical equipment.
Liu was born in a village in Yingcheng in 1953.
After finishing middle school during China's chaotic Cultural Revolution, he became a "barefoot doctor," minimally trained to work in rural areas.

name: Kazuo Okada
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2000-2024); Hurun Global (2014-2024)
forbes_bio: Kazuo Okada founded Universal Entertainment, which manufactures and sells pachinko machines and casino equipment, in 1969.
Formerly known as Aruze Corporation, Universal Entertainment trades on Tokyo's JASDAQ exchange.
The firm owns and operates the Okada Manila casino and resort in the Philippines.
forbes_facts: An art enthusiast, Okada possesses art from Japan, China and Korea, which are displayed at The Okada Museum of Art in Hakone, Japan.
Okada dropped out of high school to enroll in an engineering vocational school, and later started repairing broken jukeboxes from America.
The proposed merger between Universal Entertainment's Okada Manila and 26 Capital, a NASDAQ-listed SPAC, unravelled as both parties sued each other.

name: Meiguang Zhao
forbes_bio: Zhao Meiguang is majority shareholder of Chifeng Jilong Gold Mining, a company with interests in precious metals.

name: Pan Gang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2022); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun China (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Pan Gang chairs Shanghai-listed Inner Mongolia Yili Industrial Group, a supplier of dairy products.
Pan Gang holds a doctorate in economics from Renmin University of China, and a MBA from the China Europe International Business School.

name: Dharmesh Shah
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2023-2026); Hurun India (2017-2019); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Dharmesh Shah is the cofounder and chief technological officer of cloud-based marketing software startup HubSpot.
HubSpot went public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2014; Shah owns about 3% of the shares
He cofounded HubSpot in 2006 with the firm's executive chairman and former CEO, Brian Halligan, whom he met at MIT's business school.
Born in India and raised in the U.S., Canada and India, Shah studied computer science at Purdue and the University of Alabama.
He started his first company, Pyramid Digital Solutions, in 1994 at age 24 and later sold it to his former employer, SunGard, in 2005.

name: Shi Yifeng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2025); Hurun China (2021-2025)
forbes_bio: Shi Yifeng is general manager of Imeik Technology Development, a supplier of biomedical products.
Shi holds a MBA from elite Tsinghua University.
Imeik went public at the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2020.

name: Yuriy Kosiuk
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2011-2020); Hurun Global (2014-2020)
forbes_bio: Yuriy Kosiuk heads MHP, Ukraine's biggest producer of poultry.
He studied food process engineering at Kiev Food Industry Institute, and got his start importing furniture and gas from Turkmenistan.
He then began trading grain after the collapse of the Soviet Union, and eventually moved into poultry in 1998 with 10 employees.
Kosiuk took MHP public in 2008; he owns about 60% of the company, which trades in London.
forbes_facts: Kosiuk pays himself handsomely through dividends and has used the cash to buy airplanes, a yacht and several cars, including a Lamborghini.
